{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-de-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"13b9af4b0a5fb6a282099ffd8b55aba604c68f25e53f3e7e7ac2314cff30ed8b","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-de-class-d:lineage:54","source_registry_sha256":"7b6c7aeec232df29a8679bf39181604be2d91ce9a1cb4fcc709fed49cbe724bb","source_liveness_sha256":"53bd779b9965bd9d51630c8d8d055ccdc52a4d8ec7117a3b87241fc5129eb44f"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure","heading":"C — Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Vehicle preparation, restraint use and traffic-stop procedure

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Safe vehicle operation requires instruction and practice; a driver manual alone cannot teach the necessary skills. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Before driving, adjust the seat and mirrors, use restraints, inspect the vehicle, clear the view and secure carried items. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Trip planning includes deciding whether a trip is necessary and whether a shared ride or public transport can replace driving. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Avoiding heavy-traffic periods reduces strain and vehicle wear. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Use carpools or shared rides when practical. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Combine errands by planning destinations and tasks to reduce separate trips. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Call ahead to confirm needed goods or pickups are ready before traveling. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
Drivers are responsible for ensuring their vehicles are safe to operate. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0105]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
Follow the vehicle owner’s manual for routine maintenance, using a qualified mechanic for work that requires one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
Have brakes checked by a mechanic if they seem ineffective, make unusual noise, smell abnormal or allow the pedal to sink to the floor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
Check headlights, taillights, brake lamps and turn signals for operation from outside the vehicle. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
Brake lights communicate stopping and turn signals communicate turning to other road users. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Misaligned headlights can dazzle other drivers; persistent headlight flashes from others or poor night visibility warrant a mechanic’s check. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
Replace damaged windshield glass because it can break more readily in a minor collision or impact. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
Keep every fitted wiper working and replace blades that no longer clear water well. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Worn or bald tires can lengthen stopping distances and hinder turning on wet pavement. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
Low pressure or unbalanced tires can accelerate wear, reduce fuel efficiency and make steering or stopping harder. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Bouncing, a shaking steering wheel or pulling to one side calls for a mechanic’s inspection. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Worn tires raise the risk of hydroplaning and flat tires. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Measure tire pressure with a gauge while the tires are cold and consult the vehicle owner’s manual for the specified pressure. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
In the handbook’s penny tread check, a tire needs replacement if tread does not reach Lincoln’s head when inserted head-first. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Have steering checked if it is hard to turn or fails to respond when the wheel first moves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
Excessive bouncing after bumps or stops, or difficulty controlling the vehicle, calls for a suspension check. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
The exhaust system reduces engine noise, cools exhaust gases and carries them to the vehicle’s rear. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A02
Leaking exhaust gases can be fatal inside a vehicle in a short period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A02
Never operate an engine inside a closed garage. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A02
Have the exhaust checked periodically because many leaks cannot be heard. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0106]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A03
A commercial vehicle using an engine-compression brake needs a continuously functioning muffler meeting manufacturer specifications to prevent excessive noise. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A03
Maintain the engine according to its owner’s manual because poor running can cause power loss, poor starting or stalling in traffic. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A03
Secure loose cabin objects so they cannot strike occupants or roll beneath the brake pedal. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A03
Use the horn as a warning to other people. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A03
A load is secure only when it cannot slide, fall or shift onto the road or become airborne. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A03
Tie loads with rope, netting or straps and fasten large objects directly to the vehicle or trailer. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A03
Cover the whole load with a strong tarp or net, avoid overloading and recheck its security. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A03
Keep the windshield clean and carry cleaner with a cloth or paper towel for cleaning when needed. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A03
Keep washer fluid filled and use an antifreeze wash where freezing temperatures are possible. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A03
Clean the inner window surfaces, especially when smoking leaves a film. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A03
Remove snow, ice and frost from every window before driving. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0107]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A04
Do not hang objects from mirrors or crowd the windshield with decals that obscure vision. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F40 | anchor: A04
Keep headlamps, reversing lights, brake lights and taillights clean. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F41 | anchor: A04
Check and adjust the seat and mirrors before moving off. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F42 | anchor: A04
Set the seat high enough for a clear road view, without impairing steering, and about 12 inches from the wheel. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F43 | anchor: A04
Set mirrors to show the rear and side-window views; the handbook suggests seeing only the vehicle’s side when leaning forward slightly. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F44 | anchor: A04
Set a day/night mirror for the time of day you are driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F45 | anchor: A04
Adjust the head restraint so it meets the back of the head. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F46 | anchor: A04
Before driving away, fasten your own belt properly and ensure passengers use belts or child restraints. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F47 | anchor: A04
An officer may stop a vehicle upon seeing an occupant who is unrestrained or incorrectly restrained. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F48 | anchor: A04
Putting a shoulder belt behind the body or under the arm is improper use, can cause serious injury and can result in a ticket. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]

FACT_ID: sec12-F49 | anchor: A04
An automatic shoulder belt must still be used with the lap belt fastened. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0108]
